subject.title: fix: prune stale tool results on direct OpenAI models

question: Should direct OpenAI `cache-ttl` pruning use the existing configured pruning TTL immediately, or should it be adjusted/held until OpenAI-specific retention semantics are explicitly proven?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but merging changes upgrade behavior for existing OpenAI configs and can change which older tool-result content reaches the model after idle gaps.

options.title: Require proof and explicit TTL policy
options.body: Before merge, require redacted native OpenAI idle-gap proof and maintainer-visible documentation or tests that confirm the intended OpenAI pruning clock.

options.title: Accept existing configured TTL
options.body: Maintainers may accept that existing `contextPruning.ttl` controls OpenAI pruning even when OpenAI cache retention differs, treating this as the user's configured pruning policy.

options.title: Pause for provider-agnostic pruning
options.body: If cache-TTL remains the wrong abstraction for OpenAI, keep the canonical issue open and replace this with a provider-agnostic pruning mode.

recommendation.title: Require proof and explicit TTL policy
recommendation.body: Before merge, require redacted native OpenAI idle-gap proof and maintainer-visible documentation or tests that confirm the intended OpenAI pruning clock.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cache/pruning history and prior related review routing make this the best available owner for the OpenAI pruning policy choice.
